passage:
After a school account was stolen, the computer teacher gave a lesson on passwords. Many students used birthdays, pet names, or the same password everywhere.
The teacher introduced password managers. They could create and store strong passwords, but they also needed a strong master password and careful use.
Students learned about two-step verification and phishing messages.
One student said password rules were annoying. The teacher agreed, but compared them to locking a door. Locks are inconvenient until someone tries to enter.
Digital safety is not about fear. It is about building habits before trouble arrives.
